title: Hate Speech Classifiers Learn Human-Like Social Stereotypes

bias_targets.methodology: Correlating annotators' self-reported stereotypes, inter-annotator disagreement, and a BERT classifier's false positive/negative prediction rates with the perceived and language-embedded warmth and competence of racial identity terms (e.g., African-American, White).

Correlating annotators' self-reported stereotypes, inter-annotator disagreement, and a BERT classifier's false positive/negative prediction rates with the perceived and language-embedded warmth and competence of gender identity terms (e.g., women).

Correlating annotators' self-reported stereotypes, inter-annotator disagreement, and a BERT classifier's false positive/negative prediction rates with the perceived and language-embedded warmth and competence of religious identity terms (e.g., Muslims, Jews).

Correlating annotators' self-reported stereotypes, inter-annotator disagreement, and a BERT classifier's false positive/negative prediction rates with the perceived and language-embedded warmth and competence of sexual orientation identity terms (e.g., homosexuals, bisexuals).

Correlating annotators' self-reported stereotypes, inter-annotator disagreement, and a BERT classifier's false positive/negative prediction rates with the perceived and language-embedded warmth and competence of political/ideological identity terms (e.g., communists, liberals).

Correlating annotators' self-reported stereotypes, inter-annotator disagreement, and a BERT classifier's false positive/negative prediction rates with the perceived and language-embedded warmth and competence of nationality and immigration identity terms (e.g., immigrants).
